$comment: GENERATED from tools/cfgschema by tools/cfgdoc - do not edit; make config-docs regenerates it
title: system.toml
description: blobly_emb system configuration: the buses, cross-node signals and events, routes and node identities of a system of ECUs (docs/multi-node.md)

bus.description: the system buses, one [bus.<name>] each; the name is how signals, frames, routes and nodes refer to it

signal.description: cross-node signals, declared once at system scope (dissolution)

frame.description: SOME/IP events: id, signal set, tx mode and E2E trailer — a someip bus has no DBC to carry them

sys_bus.title: [bus.*]
sys_bus.description: One system bus: a CAN bus with its DBC, or a SOME/IP segment with its service.

interface.description: the physical channel (SocketCAN name, driver channel); unique across buses — one system bus per wire; needed where a member's own [bus.*] (its NM / telemetry bus) is matched to it

kind.description: the carrier: "can" (DBC frames) or "someip" (a service over Ethernet) Default: "can".

fd.description: CAN-FD; in a composed system it must equal each member's own [bus] fd Default: false.

bitrate.description: nominal bitrate in bit/s — informational: syscheck prints it, nothing is generated from it

dbc.description: the bus's frame contract, relative to system.toml; required on a CAN bus carrying a [[signal]], refused on someip

service.description: someip: the SOME/IP service id (required on a someip bus, refused on CAN)

version.description: someip: the interface version byte (required on a someip bus of a dissolved system, refused on CAN)

nm.description: the bus's NM cluster (CAN only); without it a node's nm id generates a disabled [nm]

sys_bus_nm.title: [bus.*.nm]
sys_bus_nm.description: An NM cluster: the alive-id range and the timings every member shares. A timing absent (or <= 0) is not lowered, so the node takes loom2v's default.

peers.description: [lo, hi] — the cluster's alive CAN ids; a member's alive id is lo + its nm; both at most 0x7FF; required when a member allocates `nm`

sys_node.title: [[node]]
sys_node.description: A member ECU and its system-owned identities.

name.description: identifier, unique; the node's generated config is gen-<name>.toml

ecu.description: the node's ecu.toml, relative to system.toml (internals only in a dissolved system)

buses.description: the system buses it sits on; more than one CAN bus makes it a [[route]] gateway Default: [].

nm.description: its NM node id (alive = peers lo + nm); absent = not an NM node; required for a ThreadX member of a bus with an NM cluster

trace.description: its trace node id, unique across the system (checked only, not generated)

diag.description: its ISO-TP diagnostic ids, unique across the system (checked only, not generated); required with `doip`

endpoint.description: its network identity: the address SOME/IP and DoIP answer at; required on a someip bus member and on a DoIP entity

doip.description: the node is a DoIP entity at its endpoint address (lowered into [doip]; dissolved systems only)

logical.description: its DoIP logical address behind a DoIP gateway that routes to it (a gateway's doip `routes`; 0x0001..0x0DFF or 0x1000..0x7FFF; unique among every logical address); needs `req` and `rsp`

address.description: IPv4 dotted quad; unique per segment; a DoIP node needs a host address of its subnet (not its network, broadcast or gateway address — on the default /24: not .0, .1 or .255)

port.description: the SOME/IP listen port (required on a someip bus; not 13400 on a DoIP node)

netmask.description: the subnet mask the node is brought up on (application and bootloader alike); contiguous, /1../30 Default: "255.255.255.0".

gateway.description: the default gateway; inside address/netmask and not its network or broadcast address. Absent = the subnet's first host, (address & netmask) | 1

sys_doip.title: [[node]] doip
sys_doip.description: The DoIP entity and its ISO 13400-2 transport policy (one parser for both files: tools/doipcfg; bounds: comm/doip policy.v).

routes.description: the nodes behind this gateway its DoIP routes diagnostics to (REQ-NET-019), at most 8: each a CAN node on a bus this node sits on, with a diag `logical`; lowered into [[doip.route]]

logical.description: the entity's logical address (0x0001..0x0DFF or 0x1000..0x7FFF); unique

functional.description: the functional address it also answers Default: 0xE400.

testers.description: tester addresses allowed to activate routing (at most 8); absent = any 0x0E00..0x0FFF

activation_types.description: routing activation types served: 0x00, 0x01, 0xE1..0xFF (at most 4) Default: [0x00].

initial_inactivity_ms.description: T_TCP_Initial_Inactivity: time to activate after the TCP connect (ms); <= general_inactivity_ms Default: 2000.

general_inactivity_ms.description: T_TCP_General_Inactivity: idle timeout once activated (ms) Default: 300000.

announce_count.description: A_DoIP_Announce_Num: vehicle announcements at start-up Default: 3.

announce_interval_ms.description: A_DoIP_Announce_Interval (ms); count x interval at most 10000 ms Default: 500.

route_level.description: a gateway's: the security level of its own server a tester must have unlocked over the network before it routes to the nodes behind it (REQ-NET-020); one its [uds] serves Default: 1.

allow_bench_key.description: answer 0x27 with blobly_net's PUBLIC reference key over the network — a bench posture, opted into by name; required (true) when [uds] security_key = "reference" Default: false.

sys_signal.title: [[signal]]
sys_signal.description: A cross-node signal, declared exactly once: who produces it, on which bus and in which frame.

name.description: the signal name; FBs read and write it by this name

fields.description: payload fields, name -> scalar type (bool, u8/i8, u16/i16, u32/i32, f32, f64; u64/i64 not on CAN); one value field on CAN

producer.description: the node that transmits it; must be on `bus` and have an FB that writes it

frame.description: CAN: the DBC message carrying it (sent by the producer); someip: the [[frame]] event carrying it

cycle_ms.description: CAN tx cadence (ms); signals sharing a frame must agree; refused on someip (the [[frame]] tx says it) Default: 100.

sys_frame.title: [[frame]]
sys_frame.description: A SOME/IP event on a someip bus: its id, its signals and how it is sent. Lowering copies only what it recognises, so an unknown key is refused.

name.description: the event name; unique per bus

bus.description: the someip bus it is on

id.description: the SOME/IP event id (bit 15 set; methods own 0x0001..0x7FFF); unique per bus

signals.description: its payload signals, in packing order; non-empty, all on the same bus

tx.description: how the producer sends it; absent = cyclic every 100 ms

mode.description: how the producer sends it: periodically, on a change, or both (the event modes SOME/IP generates) Default: "cyclic".

cycle_ms.description: the cadence (ms) of a cyclic or mixed event Default: 100.

min_delay_ms.description: the least gap between two event sends (ms) Default: 0.

counter_pos.description: the counter's byte: the appended trailer starts at the derived payload size

crc_pos.description: the CRC's byte, right after the counter

timeout_ms.description: the receiver's sender-loss timeout (ms), longer than the cycle; required unless mode = "event"

sys_route.title: [[route]]
sys_route.description: A gateway route between two buses (dissolution only): set exactly one of `frame` / `signal`.

gateway.description: the node that forwards; it must sit on both buses

frame.description: a raw frame route: the DBC message forwarded as it is (in both DBCs; not on an FD bus); this or `signal`, exactly one

signal.description: a signal route: the [[signal]] decoded on `from` and re-encoded on `to`; this or `frame`, exactly one
